Interpolation ?
🎬 Interpolation

Uses AI to generate smooth motion between frames.

  • 1 image + ON: Natural talking motion
  • Multiple + ON: Smooth transitions
  • OFF: Static/minimal motion

✓ Recommended: Keep ON

📌 In Storyboard mode, this is controlled per-scene.
AI Prompts ?
🤖 AI Prompts

Let AI analyze images and optimize prompts.

  • Visual analysis: Camera, lighting, scene
  • Voice profile: Matches subject
  • Gestures: Natural movements

Turn OFF to write custom prompt.
Short Lines ?
📝 Short Dialogue Mode

How to handle dialogue lines under 13 words:

  • Timed: 2s speech + silent action for remaining time (default)
  • Fill: Pad with filler words to 25 words for continuous speech

Fill mode avoids awkward silence but may sound unnatural at the end.
Prefix Short ?
🔤 Prefix Short Lines

Prepend a leading word (e.g. "only") to dialogue lines shorter than the threshold.

Useful when Veo clips the first consonant of a clip's first word at scene boundaries — the prefix gives Veo a throwaway onset to "warm up" on, so the real first word survives the cut.

  • Stacks with Timed or Fill — independent setting
  • Threshold counts only the original line (default: under 15 words)
  • Prefix word and threshold are both customizable

Applied to BOTH the Veo prompt AND the WhisperVAD script — so silence-removal won't cut the prefix back out.
Prefix word
Apply if line has < N words
Gesture Enrichment ?
🤌 Gesture Enrichment

AI generates content-specific gestures matching what's being said.

  • Mentions head: points at head
  • Mentions mixing: stirring motion
  • Lists 3 things: holds up 3 fingers

Uses 1 extra OpenAI call per clip (~$0.001/clip).
Generation Mode ?
⚡ Generation Mode

Choose how clips are processed:

  • 🔀 Smart (Staggered): Odd clips (1,3,5) first in parallel, then even clips (2,4) use confirmed frames.
  • ⚡ Fast (Parallel): All clips at once. Fastest, but may have gaps.
  • 🔗 Safe (Sequential): One at a time. Slowest but most reliable.

Tip: install Kaveno as an app (Chrome address bar → install icon) to make folder permission persist across sessions. Otherwise re-click Pick folder once each session.

Pick a local folder. While this tab is open we poll every ~30s, find new .mp4 / .mov / .webm files, upload them and auto-match against jobs in Finishing. Matched jobs move to Published before the Instagram sync runs — when the reel posts the IG URL fills in automatically.

Don't rename the file. The exported filename already carries its job id, so dropping it in as-is makes the match exact — rename it and we have to guess from the audio.

Browser support: Chrome / Edge / Opera. Firefox / Safari can't watch folders.

📋 Import scene table

Paste a markdown scene table. Each ### Scene N block becomes a generated node. The reference_image field creates parent→child links between scenes. The subject you pick below is attached to every scene as the "image 1" subject.
How the build markdown is structured

The importer reads your build file. It has up to three sections:

  • ## Ingredients — a table naming your uploads (the character = your subject, an optional product). Optional, used to bind the product upload by name.
  • ## Images — one ### Image N per image to generate. - **reference_image:** is none or image_K (a lower number, to build on an earlier image). The prompt goes in a fenced block under - **Image prompt:**.
  • ## Storyboard — one ### Scene N per clip. It points at an image with - **image:** image_N and carries the spoken - **line:** + - **action_note:**.
  • ## Veo 3.1 Final Prompts — the per-clip video prompt (what gets passed to Veo when the build is generated / promoted to video). One ### Clip N.M per clip, with **Start frame:** Image N + a fenced **Text prompt:**.
Inside the Image prompt (the prompt format)

Each fenced **Image prompt:** follows the build convention — labelled sections then quality rules:
[Composition] [Subject] [Action] [Location] [Style] [Tech] then a POSITIVE: line and one or more [...] NEGATIVE: lines. The whole block is sent to Nano Banana as the prompt. Your Prompt prefix (below) is prepended to every scene.

Inside a Veo clip prompt (the prompt you actually pass per clip)

Each ### Clip N.M — Scene N, Line M (REGISTER) has **Start frame:** Image N (ties the clip to its image) then a fenced **Text prompt:**: a camera line → the action across the clip → the spoken line inline (says in a <tone> voice, "…") → Ambient: → (no subtitles, no captions). No separate Negative prompt block — bans are written affirmatively into the text (standing rule).

## Images

### Image 1
- **reference_image:** none
- **Image prompt:**
```
Use the uploaded character reference image for the main character.

[Composition] iPhone wide-angle, 9:16. The main character chest-up holding a small amber jar.
[Subject] The main character, warm confident expression, eyes to the lens.
[Action] She lifts the jar toward the camera.
[Location] Sunlit American kitchen, marble island, blurred shelves behind.
[Style] Natural HDR daylight, warm palette, photorealistic.
[Tech] iPhone wide-angle, deep focus, 2K, 9:16.
POSITIVE: one unified photorealistic image, correct proportions, natural skin detail.
[ANATOMY] NEGATIVE: no extra fingers, no distorted anatomy, no text, no watermark.
```

### Image 2
- **reference_image:** image_1
- **visual_delta:** same kitchen + persona; now pouring the jar into a glass of warm milk.
- **Image prompt:**
```
Use the uploaded character reference image for the main character.

[Composition] Chest-up, close on her hands over a glass of warm milk on the counter.
[Action] She pours the jar into the warm milk.
[Location] Same kitchen.
[Style] Natural HDR daylight, photorealistic.
[Tech] iPhone wide-angle, deep focus, 2K, 9:16.
POSITIVE: one unified photorealistic image, natural skin + liquid detail.
[ANATOMY] NEGATIVE: no extra fingers, no distorted anatomy, no text, no watermark.
```

## Veo 3.1 Final Prompts (per clip)

### Clip 1.1 — Scene 1, Line 1 (HOOK)
**Start frame:** Image 1
**Text prompt:**
```
Static handheld camera, slight natural drift.

Across the clip, the main character lifts the jar toward the camera, then locks eyes to the lens through the line.

The main character says in a warm, confident voice, "here's the one thing nobody tells you."

Ambient: quiet sunlit kitchen room tone.
(no subtitles, no captions)
```

### Clip 2.1 — Scene 2, Line 1 (RECIPE)
**Start frame:** Image 2
**Text prompt:**
```
Static handheld camera, slight natural drift.

Across the clip, the main character pours the jar into the warm milk, then glances to the lens.

The main character says in a warm, teaching voice, "pour it into warm milk and drink it before bed."

Ambient: same kitchen room tone, soft pour sound.
(no subtitles, no captions)
```
An image with reference_image: image_1 waits in draft until you pick a chosen variant of image 1 — then it auto-queues. Legacy files that use ### Scene N with an inline Image prompt (no ### Image N) still import too.
How scheduling works: Scenes without a reference_image start queuing immediately. Scenes that reference an earlier scene stay in draft until you pick a chosen variant of their parent — only then do they auto-queue. This ensures each scene in a chain is built from an approved predecessor.
